claims.claim: For every signed orthogonal frame, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected one of the two advertised knight encounter branches lie in the finite grid, that selected branch is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(q+r;a,r,f).
claims.evidence: From C0=(q+r,q+2r,q+2r+f), the first branch proceeds through (q+r,q+2r+f,q+r+f) to (q+r+a,q+3r+f,q+r). The second proceeds through (q+r,q+2r+f,q+3r+f), then (q+r,q+r+f,q+3r+f), and finally (q+r+a,q+r,q+3r+f). Because a,r,f are signed units on distinct axes, every labeled displacement is unit or idle, every configuration has three distinct nodes, and no pair traverses one edge in opposite directions. Both final sets equal {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). If every displayed node is a grid vertex, each unit displacement is a source-grid edge. Translation by q preserves all checks. Exhaustive integer enumeration passed all 48 frames and two branches, totaling 96 traces.
claims.search_method: Algebraic trace verification plus exhaustive enumeration of all 96 frame-branch cases.

claims.claim: The finite-grid node-existence hypothesis in the revised knight-encounter claim is necessary in the source model.
claims.evidence: Source-model configurations contain only grid vertices. In V={0,1,2,3}^3, the supplied staging triple is valid, but q+3r+f=(4,1,0) is outside V. That node occurs in both advertised branches—immediately in the outward branch and later in the inward branch—so staging-node existence alone cannot make either complete branch a source-grid trace.
claims.search_method: Direct exact-coordinate evaluation of both branches in the stated 4x4x4 grid.

claims.claim: At the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected choice lie in the finite grid, that choice is collision-free and swap-free and yields the stated diagonal frame.
claims.evidence: With {d,e}={a,-r}, d,e,f are signed units on distinct axes. From (q,q+d,q+f), the e-choice goes directly to (q,q+d,q+e+f), whose set is D(q;d,e,f). The d-choice goes through (q,q+d,q+d+f) and then (q+e,q,q+d+f), whose set is D(q;e,d,f). Every displacement is unit or idle, destinations remain distinct, and no reversed-edge swap occurs. Conditional node existence therefore makes every movement a legal grid edge. Exhaustive integer enumeration passed 48 frames, two d/e orders, and two choices, totaling 192 cases.
claims.search_method: Algebraic trace verification plus exhaustive enumeration of all 192 frame-order-choice cases.

claims.claim: From the advertised outer-reset staging configuration, whenever all nodes displayed by a selected edge choice, short-axis choice, and conversion sign lie in the finite grid, that selected trace is collision-free and swap-free and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
claims.evidence: Let s=q+d. The shift takes (q,q+d,q+2d) to (s,s+d,s+d+x). For sign +d, the subsequent configurations are (s,s+d+x,s+2d+x), (s,s+x,s+2d+x), and (s+y,s,s+2d+x). For sign -d they are (s,s+d+x,s+x), (s,s+2d+x,s+x), and (s+y,s+2d+x,s). Since d,x,y are signed units on three distinct axes, each movement is unit or idle, each destination triple is distinct, and no two labeled paths reverse the same edge. Both final sets are {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Conditional node existence supplies grid legality. Exhaustive integer enumeration passed 48 frames, two d/e orders, two x/y orders, and two signs, totaling 384 traces.
claims.search_method: Algebraic trace verification plus exhaustive enumeration of all 384 parameter combinations.

claims.claim: The reset recurrence h=-f, {d,e}={a,-r}, {x,y}={h,e}, (a,r,f)->(y,d,x) is closed on the 48 signed orthogonal frames for all four choices.
claims.evidence: For any input frame, d and e reorder a and -r, while h=-f lies on the remaining axis. Then x and y reorder h and e. Consequently (y,d,x) contains exactly one signed unit from each coordinate axis and is another member of the 48-frame set. Exhaustive integer enumeration confirmed all 48×2×2=192 recurrence edges.
claims.search_method: Direct structural proof and exhaustive enumeration of all 192 recurrence choices.

claims.claim: The exact target remains unresolved by this draft.
claims.evidence: The construction route requires an at-most-76-shade algorithm A=(Cl,Init,T) and proof that every self-inconsistent adversarial execution perpetually explores every allowed finite grid. The draft supplies no shade-state definitions, Init, total local-view transition function, reachability argument, or universal coverage proof. The alternative route requires excluding every algorithm using at most 76 shades, but no such lower bound is presented. Local conditional coordinate lemmas and frame closure establish neither route.
claims.search_method: Manual comparison of every draft result and the final writeup against both disjuncts and all quantifiers of the exact source target.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either a complete ambiguous visibility-one PEP algorithm for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades, or a proof that 77 shades are necessary. The draft proves neither. Its exact arithmetic, conditional safety/endpoint lemmas, boundary counterexamples, and recurrence-closure lemma are correct, nonvacuous, and relevant to a possible construction, so they constitute valid but limited partial progress. They do not define Cl, Init, or T; establish local recognizability or staging reachability; handle all boundary cases; prove termination under every adversarial transformation sequence; or prove perpetual coverage. Nor is there a 76-shade impossibility argument. The draft claims only PARTIAL and its headline/final writeup explicitly says the target remains open, so claimed_resolution is accurate and not overstated.
